newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul prosecutors prepare arrest of president's son.
newsitem.headline: Seoul prosecutors prepare arrest of president's son.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors on Thursday prepared to arrest one of President Kim Young-sam's sons over a sleaze scandal revealed by the collapse of failed Hanbo Steel Co, prosecution sources said.
Kim Hyun-chul, the president's second son, has been ordered to appear at the prosecution office at 2.00 p.m. (0500 GMT) on Thursday for questioning over allegations of bribery and influence-peddling.
"He has been summoned as a suspect," a prosecution official told reporters. "Prosecutors have secured enough evidence that the president's son violated laws."
He gave no further details but prosecution sources said said Kim Hyun-chul was expected to be arrested this week.
During parliamentary hearings over a loans-for-kickbanks scandal surrounding Hanbo, Kim Hyun-chul denied he took bribes from companies or meddled in state affairs.
South Korean prosecutors have traditionally announced the summoning of suspected criminals only when they have secured evidence to charge them.
"Kim Hyun-chul is not an exception. He will face legal action if any wrongdoing is found," a prosecution spokesman said.

Prosecutors said they had traced more than 100 bank accounts of Kim Hyun-chul's close associates and their relatives to find out if the president's son accepted kickbacks in return for peddling influence.

Senior prosecutor Shim Je-ryoon said Kim Hyun-chul had received 60 million won ($67,000) each from three companies every month between mid-1993 and late 1995. Shim did not say if the money was bribes.

Kim Hyun-chul, the first son of an South Korean incumbent president being probed for criminal offences, was questioned by prosecutors in February over accusations that he pressured banks to keep loans rolling to Hanbo Steel.
Hanbo Steel, South Korea's second largest steelmaker, folded in January under debt of five trillion won, to shed light on a web of corrupt alliances beteen politicians, businessmen and bankers.

Prosecutors have exonerated Kim Hyun-chul over the Hanbo scandal for which 11 people are on trial, including a former cabinet minister, president's aids, ruling and opposition lawmakers, bankers and Hanbo founder Chung Tae-soo.

Kim Hyun-chul's two business associates -- Park Tae-joong and Kim Hi-chan -- have been arrested on charges of taking bribes in return for promises to lobby the younger Kim to help obtain government broadcast licences.
Kim Hyun-chul, who helped engineer his father's win in the 1992 presidential election, is also under investigation over allegations that he had kept part of unspent election campaign funds.

The main opposition National Congress for New Politics party has alleged Kim Hyun-chul pressured banks to provide loans to Hanbo in return for a donation worth tens of billions of won to help finance the 1992 campaign. Kim has denied this.
Financing of the 1992 vote and the Hanbo scandal have emerged as the most explosive political issues in the run-up to the presidential elections in December.
President Kim's five-year single term expires next February and he is barred by the constitution from seeking re-election. ($1 = 893 won)
